props.title: The Da Vinci Code
props.initialSlug: The Truth Will Set You Free

sections.content: **The Da Vinci Code** (2006) sparked a global phenomenon by translating Dan Brown's controversial bestseller into a high-stakes religious thriller. Tom Hanks leads as Robert Langdon, establishing a template for cerebral treasure hunts that influenced films like **National Treasure** (2004) and **Angels & Demons** (2009). Director Ron Howard crafts an atmospheric journey through European landmarks, though the film's dense exposition and religious conspiracy theories generated significant backlash from the Catholic Church, similar to the controversy surrounding **The Last Temptation of Christ** (1988).

sections.content: The film exemplifies Hollywood's fascination with religious mysteries and ancient conspiracies, following a tradition established by **Raiders of the Lost Ark** (1981) and continued through **Inferno** (2016). Its blend of academic detective work and action sequences created a distinct subgenre of intellectual thrillers, influencing works like **The Lost Symbol** (2021) and **Uncharted** (2022). The film's extensive use of real locations and historical references, though historically questionable, set a standard for mixing fact and fiction in mainstream entertainment. SUBHEAD: Religious Controversy and Cultural Impact

While **The Da Vinci Code** (2006) faced criticism for its historical accuracy, it opened doors for more films exploring alternative religious histories, like **Kingdom of Heaven** (2005) and **Assassin's Creed** (2016). The film's success demonstrated audiences' appetite for conspiracy theories wrapped in historical packaging, though later entries like **Angels & Demons** (2009) and **Inferno** (2016) never matched its cultural impact. Howard's direction emphasizes puzzle-solving over action, creating a more cerebral thriller that influenced television series like **The Lost Symbol** (2021) and **Decoded** (2010).
